report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of graph_brief.py: verified layer rendering, budget accounting, docstring claims; all claims kept or uncheckable.
risks: graph_brief.py:281-376 | medium | Budget accounting for header: comment says header space reserved up front but code adds header to text after rendering; if header exceeds budget, final text may exceed budget_chars. | Check if header length is included in spent before rendering layers or if final text length is enforced.

graph_brief.py:299-307 | low | _emit adds head length to spent only after appending lines; if head itself exceeds remaining budget, it still gets added, potentially causing overshoot. | Verify if head size is checked against budget before adding.

graph_brief.py:361-373 | low | DOCUMENTS layer uses wiki.items() sorted by page; if wiki is not a dict but a Mapping with different iteration order, sorted() handles it, but type assumption may be fragile. | Confirm wiki_code_links is always a dict-like with string keys.

graph_brief.py:410-415 | low | render_brief catches all exceptions and returns ''; if graph_brief raises a programming error, it is silently swallowed, potentially hiding bugs. | Consider logging or re-raising in debug mode.

handoff.purpose: Render budgeted structural brief layers (imports, symbols, documents), assemble header and return GraphBrief; provide render_brief convenience wrapper.

symbols.name: _emit
symbols.note: Closure inside graph_brief; renders a layer if it fits within budget_chars, tracking spent and dropped lines.

symbols.name: render_brief
symbols.note: Returns graph_brief(...).text or '' on any exception.

claims.text: The header is written last but must not escape the budget, so its space is reserved up front.
claims.why: The chunk shows _HEADER_RESERVE used to initialize spent, but does not show its definition or how the final header length is accounted; cannot verify against this chunk alone.

claims.text: Called in PRIORITY order, not display order.
claims.why: The code calls _emit for imports, symbols, documents in that order (lines 324, 350, 378), while display order is symbols, imports, documents (line 398).

claims.text: Small high-value layers are rendered first and DISPLAYED in reading order.
claims.why: Imports rendered first (line 324), then symbols (line 350), then documents (line 378); display reorders to symbols, imports, documents (line 398).

claims.text: the 1-hop symbol layer around offload.py alone is 495 lines, and emitting it first consumed the entire budget and dropped the import layer
claims.why: The claim references a specific measured scenario outside this chunk; no data in the chunk verifies the line count or the historical behavior.

claims.text: Artefact importers are filtered HERE as well as in the neighbourhood.
claims.why: Line 319 filters reverse edges with _is_artefact, and line 314 filters forward edges with _is_artefact.

claims.text: a reverse edge is read straight off the index and never passed through the walk.
claims.why: The code uses reverse.get(rel) directly from the index (line 319) without passing through _neighbourhood.

claims.text: '->' imports, '<-' is imported by.
claims.why: Forward edges are rendered as 'rel -> deps' (line 315), reverse as 'rel <- imported by ...' (line 321).

claims.text: '{DEEP_EDGE_MARK}' marks an edge that exists only inside a function body -- a change there still breaks the importer.
claims.why: DEEP_EDGE_MARK is not defined in this chunk; the semantics of the mark cannot be verified here.

claims.text: PUBLIC API ONLY for a neighbour. What a caller may use from another module is its public surface; its private helpers are not callable and listing them cost 495 lines around offload.py
claims.why: Line 349 calls file_symbols(path, include_private=False) for neighbours, whereas line 334 calls file_symbols(path) without that flag for targets.

claims.text: If a name is not listed under its file, it does not exist in that file. Do not import it.
claims.why: The symbols layer lists only symbols returned by file_symbols; absence implies not listed, but the claim is a directive, not a verifiable fact.

claims.text: document_links_reverse is keyed BY THE CODE FILE, which is the lookup wanted here
claims.why: Line 365 uses rev.get(rel) where rel is a code file path from rels.

claims.text: Both keys are absent unless the document layer is enabled, so this section vanishes rather than lying when it is off.
claims.why: The chunk shows the section is guarded by include_docs (line 358), but whether the index keys are absent when disabled is not observable here.

claims.text: Wikilinks from a page INTO code are a separate relation with its own layer, and are only forward-keyed.
claims.why: The code uses wiki.items() (line 372) and filters hits against rels, treating wiki as a forward map from page to code files.

claims.text: A page that describes one of these files. Its claims are a PROMISE, not evidence -- where the code disagrees, the document is the bug.
claims.why: The note is a policy statement; the code renders document references without validating their claims.

claims.text: This describes SHAPE, not behaviour. Never cite it as evidence about what code does.
claims.why: The header text is included in the output as written.

claims.text: BUDGET: truncated -- ... Absence below is NOT evidence of absence in the repo.
claims.why: The header appends the truncated message when dropped is non-empty (line 393).

claims.text: DISPLAY order, independent of the priority order the layers were rendered in: symbols first because 'what exists' is what a writer needs before anything else, then who reaches whom, then what has been promised.
claims.why: Line 398 constructs sections in the order ('symbols', 'imports', 'documents').

claims.text: No structural facts available for these files.
claims.why: Line 401 appends this when sections is empty.

claims.text: :func:`graph_brief` as text, or "" if there is nothing to say.
claims.why: Returns graph_brief(...).text (line 415) or '' on exception (line 417).

claims.text: it must never raise into a lane, so a failure to describe the graph degrades to no description.
claims.why: The try/except catches all exceptions (line 416) and returns '' (line 417).

observations.what: The budget accounting for the header is not fully verified: _HEADER_RESERVE is used to initialize spent, but the final header is assembled after layers are rendered and its length is not checked against the budget.

In _emit, the head length is added to spent only after lines are appended; if head itself exceeds the remaining budget, it is still added, potentially causing the rendered layer to exceed budget_chars.
The DOCUMENTS layer uses wiki.items() and sorts by page; if wiki is not a dict but some other Mapping, sorted() may fail if keys are not comparable, but typical string keys are fine.
render_brief silently swallows all exceptions, which could hide programming errors in graph_brief.
